title: Your first Apple app, from idea to support
introduction: Build one useful task on one primary device first. Add other Apple surfaces when they help that task. Each phase has a small piece of evidence that tells you when to move on.

phases.title: Set up the workspace
phases.goal: Make your work reproducible before you make screens.

actions.text: Install and open a compatible Xcode release on a Mac.
Put the project under source control and record the Xcode and SDK versions.
Run a tiny starter app in Simulator; use a physical device when the feature depends on hardware.

If paid distribution is planned, enroll early; have the Account Holder accept the latest Paid Apps Agreement and complete tax and banking information before building the purchase flow. Apple source checked 2026-09-27: https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-agreements/sign-and-update-agreements

Before fixing the app name, clear the chosen name and marks in the intended storefront regions and decide whether the public seller will be an individual or legal organization. Apple seller-name source checked 2026-09-27: https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/program-enrollment/

phases.output: A clean checkout that another person could open and run.
phases.failure: Tool versions, signing, or missing assets make later builds fail only on another machine.
phases.recovery: Write down the toolchain and build steps now; keep credentials out of the repository.

phases.title: Find a repeated problem
phases.goal: Choose a job people already try to complete.

actions.text: Describe the person and the moment the problem appears.
Watch or ask a few people how they handle it today.
Write down the free Apple feature or existing app you must beat.

phases.output: A one-sentence user problem with evidence from real behavior.
phases.failure: A clever feature is built before anyone needs it, so there is no reason to return.
phases.recovery: Narrow the idea to one recurring moment and ask people about their current workaround.

phases.title: Promise one useful result
phases.goal: Know what the person gets in the first session and why they would come back.

actions.text: Write the first useful result in plain language.
Describe the repeat-use trigger and the smallest version that delivers it.
Choose free, one-time, or subscription value only after the ongoing job is clear.

phases.output: A brief with first result, return loop, success measure, and non-goals.
phases.failure: Scope expands faster than proof of value, while pricing is chosen from benchmarks rather than this product.
phases.recovery: Cut the first release back to one complete result and treat pricing as a hypothesis.

phases.title: Choose the first device
phases.goal: Start where the job is easiest to perform well.

actions.text: Pick one primary platform and minimum OS version.
List what each additional device would uniquely contribute and choose representative hardware for performance checks.
Check APIs, entitlements, permissions, and hardware before promising a surface.

phases.output: A platform and capability matrix with one primary target.
phases.failure: Supporting every device from day one creates many layouts and tests before the core job works.
phases.recovery: Keep shared meaning and data, but add native device presentations one at a time.

phases.title: Draw the complete journey
phases.goal: Make the action understandable from entry through success and recovery.

actions.text: Draw launch, first action, result, repeat use, and exit.
For each important action, specify button label, feedback, failure, retry, and undo.
Include empty, offline, permission-denied, and accessibility paths that apply.

phases.output: A flowchart, action contracts, and state inventory.
phases.failure: Happy-path screens look polished while errors or permissions strand the user.
phases.recovery: Walk the journey with a novice and deliberately trigger a failure before adding polish.

phases.title: Choose a visual identity
phases.goal: Make the product recognizable while keeping native behavior clear.

actions.text: Select a personality recipe and define semantic colors, type, copy, and motion.
Use native Liquid Glass navigation and controls where supported; keep the content layer clear and define an earlier-OS fallback.
Brief the app icon from the product promise; explore several concepts.
Preview light, dark, contrast, reduced transparency, larger text, reduced motion, and icon variants.

phases.output: Identity decisions, design tokens, editable icon source, and reviewed previews.
phases.failure: A pretty mockup hides weak labels, low contrast, or an icon that disappears at small size.
phases.recovery: Test native controls and actual-size icon previews before custom styling spreads.

phases.title: Create the app foundation
phases.goal: Make the smallest native project that can run and evolve.

actions.text: Create the app target, bundle identifier, scene, assets, and focused tests.
Choose local storage and data ownership before adding sync or accounts.
Add an extension or entitlement only for a selected capability.

phases.output: A running native app with recorded project settings and an empty-state preview.
phases.failure: Premature packages, backends, and extensions slow every change and increase signing failures.
phases.recovery: Remove unused layers and make the first target build cleanly before adding another.

phases.title: Build one complete task
phases.goal: Ship a thin path from launch to the promised result.

actions.text: Implement the action and its real state transitions.
Make data durable enough for the job and preserve user work on failure.
Run it on the primary device and fix confusing points.

phases.output: A demonstrated useful result, including a failure and recovery route.
phases.failure: Many half-built features create activity without a usable product.
phases.recovery: Stop starting new surfaces until one journey is complete end to end.

phases.title: Add useful system surfaces
phases.goal: Let people reach the same job in the right context.

actions.text: Select widgets, Live Activities, Watch, Mac commands, App Intents, sharing, or notifications only for a specific job.
Define each surface's lifecycle, privacy, fallback, and tap destination.
Test it on supported hardware and with the main app unavailable or suspended.

phases.output: A verified module contract for every selected system surface.
phases.failure: Extensions, background rules, and refresh budgets are assumed to behave like the foreground app.
phases.recovery: Treat each surface as an independent delivery path with its own limits and diagnostics.

phases.title: Test the whole experience
phases.goal: Find failures before a stranger does.

actions.text: Test the core result, restart, offline, denied permissions, large text, VoiceOver, and localization.
Review Liquid Glass legibility and input behavior in each selected platform and appearance.
Measure launch, interaction hitches, memory, energy, and long-session behavior on representative physical devices; compare with a recorded baseline.
Check data lifecycle, privacy declarations, and crashes; run purchase and restore tests if the app sells digital goods.

phases.output: A test matrix with device, OS, build, result, and remaining risks.
phases.failure: Simulator success is mistaken for device, account, network, or distribution success.
phases.recovery: Reproduce critical paths on hardware and record exactly what was and was not checked.

phases.title: Put it in testers' hands
phases.goal: Learn what happens when you are not guiding the user.

actions.text: Prepare signing and an App Store Connect record for TestFlight where applicable.
Give testers a task, not a tour of the features.
Collect confusion, crashes, failed results, and repeated requests.

phases.output: A triaged beta feedback list and a stable release candidate.
phases.failure: Friendly testers say the app looks good while the core job remains hard to finish.
phases.recovery: Observe task completion and fix the most repeated block before adding features.

phases.title: Prepare and ship honestly
phases.goal: Make the build, listing, payment, privacy, and support promise agree.

actions.text: Prepare screenshots, description, support and privacy URLs, rating, regions, and review access.
Check signed build, entitlements, app icon, purchases, restore, and export compliance as applicable.
Choose App Store release or a direct Mac distribution path and complete its requirements.

phases.output: An approved release candidate with a complete distribution checklist.
phases.failure: Store metadata or signing describes a different app than the one submitted.
phases.recovery: Run the reviewer path from a clean install and compare every claim with the final build.

phases.title: Support and improve it
phases.goal: Keep the app useful after launch.

actions.text: Watch crashes, support requests, reviews, performance, and repeat task completion.
Fix reliability and confusing recovery before expanding scope.
Review each new OS and device for compatibility and update the app's promises.

phases.output: A support loop, release notes, compatibility record, and next evidence-based change.
phases.failure: The app ships once, then OS changes and unresolved customer friction accumulate.
phases.recovery: Reserve time for maintenance and let observed problems choose the next iteration.
